title: Disaster Recovery Runbooks & RTO / RPO
description: Design Disaster Recovery (DR) plans, meet RTO and RPO metrics, and execute multi-region failover tests.

data.text: A database high-availability architecture is useless without documented, tested Disaster Recovery (DR) runbooks. DR strategy is defined by two fundamental metrics: **RTO** and **RPO**.

rows: How long can the application be down before recovery?
How much data loss (in time) is acceptable?

items.text: Automated WAL segment shipping to offsite cold storage (S3/GCS)
items.hint: Protects against entire data center destruction

items.text: Quarterly game day drills testing database recovery from scratch
Documented runbook with explicit DNS/connection string failover steps
items.hint: Do not invent failover steps during an outage

items.text: Alerts for replication lag exceeding 10 seconds

data.text: Turning RPO into an Archiving Command

The RPO you promise is set by how often WAL is archived. Continuous archiving with `archive_command` and retention in object storage gives an RPO of seconds; a nightly `pg_dump` gives an RPO of a day. The runbook must name the exact recovery command so that a stressed operator at 3 AM is not improvising.

data.title: Continuous archiving and a restore command
data.content: WAL segments are copied offsite as they complete; recovery replays them until the target time, then stops.
data.code:
# postgresql.conf: ship every completed WAL segment offsite
archive_mode = on
archive_command = 'aws s3 cp %p s3://pg-wal-archive/%f'
archive_timeout = 60s      # force a segment switch at least every 60s

# recovery: replay archived WAL into a restored base backup
restore_command = 'aws s3 cp s3://pg-wal-archive/%f %p'
recovery_target_time = '2024-05-01 14:14:00+00'
recovery_target_action = 'promote'

data.title: Interview angle: state RTO and RPO before the technology
data.text: Interviewers ask about disaster recovery to see whether you start from requirements. The strong answer states the RTO (how long the outage may last) and the RPO (how much data loss is acceptable) first, then chooses the mechanism: PITR with WAL archiving for a low RPO, a hot standby in another region for a low RTO, or both. Finish by saying that an untested runbook is not a recovery plan, which is why game-day drills matter.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RTO measures downtime duration; RPO measures data loss window.
Regular game day recovery rehearsals are mandatory.
Offsite WAL archiving guarantees data survival even if the primary cloud region fails.
